exclusion_detail: Aldehyde inferred from the product name, glycosylation conditions conflict between two sections, the NMR for the lead looks unreliable, lead co-named (second reader). (Reclassified 2026-10-24 after the verification pass.)

lead.why: The abstract names no single best compound; rule 2: 27 is the most potent inhibitor in Table 1 (AChE IC50 2.05, BChE 5.42 uM) and the paper's docking highlight ('visualization of most potent compound 27', Figs. 5 and 6).

reactions.conditions: 2-Hydroxyacetophenone (10 mmol) in MeOH + 10 mL 30% NaOH, stirred 30 min; aldehyde (10 mmol) added dropwise, stirred 24 h (Claisen-Schmidt).

35% H2O2 (1.5 mL) added to the same basic methanolic mixture, stirred 1 h (Algar-Flynn-Oyamada oxidative cyclisation); acidified with 10% HCl, precipitate filtered, washed, dried, crystallised from EtOH; used directly in the next step.

Flavonol (1.0 mmol), K2CO3 (3 equiv), TBAB (3 equiv) in CHCl3 (5 mL) + H2O (5 mL), 30 min; peracetylglycosyl bromide (1.5 equiv) added, rt 36 h (phase-transfer glycosylation); neutralised with 10% HCl, extracted with DCM, column chromatography (petroleum ether/EtOAc). Yield for 27: 83%.

alt_variants.conditions: One-pot reading of the general procedure: NaOH/MeOH aldol condensation 24 h, then H2O2 added to the same flask for 1 h (chalcone not isolated).

notes: (1) The paper gives ONE general procedure for all of 21-30 and never names 4-isobutylbenzaldehyde for 27; the aldehyde is derived from the printed name of 27 (2-(4-isobutylphenyl)). Neither intermediate has a printed name. (2) Section 3.1 describes the glycosylation in K2CO3/DMF but Section 2.1 gives CHCl3/H2O with TBAB; I used the experimental one. (3) Section 3.1 calls chalcone formation + AFO a 'two steps sequence', while Section 2.1 runs them in one flask; main = 3 steps, alt = 2. (4) The sugar stereo SMILES (beta-D-glucoside from alpha-D-bromide, as the name states) was written by hand and not machine-checked. (5) The reported NMR/13C data for 27 look internally inconsistent (e.g. 13C 192.2 for the flavone C=O), but the structure follows the printed name. No usable SI text (NMR spectra only).
